title: A matcher that scores function words looks like cross-domain discovery and is noise
problem: Does the library link experiences from different domains that share one underlying mechanism -- the stated ambition for it?
failure: It appeared to. Three cards from three domains (API capability, audio render determinism, a typed zero in a binomial measurement table) that share one mechanism were all three returned by abstract queries such as `measured a proxy instead of the thing itself`. But those three cards share, as content tokens, only `a an is not the`. The scorer counts every shared token, so the link came from function words. Proof: the query `the a of is not an` returns all three with scores 13/11/9; `and the of to a in that it is not` returns all three at 17/13/10; `the xqzzy wobble flurb` returns all three while `xqzzy wobble flurb` returns none. The pure-function-word query `the a instead of is not an itself thing` scores HIGHER (14/11/11) than the meaningful query it was derived from (10/9/8). The same defect defeats ARGO's independent negative control in evaluation/BILINGUAL_BASELINE_2026-11-26.md: `music composition` correctly scores 0, but `the music composition` returns all three fixture cards, and `a music composition is not` returns them at top score 8. The two defects also intersect -- `المصادقة` returns nothing (D1) while `the المصادقة` returns all three (D2).
correction: Not applied here -- HERMUZ's lane, and ARGO's baseline states Claude owns solution exploration while ARGO contributes the baseline. Proposed: discount a function-word list in both languages before scoring, and score content-token overlap only, so a card sharing no content token with the query is not returned however many articles it matches. Keep the empty-meaning queries as a permanent soundness suite: a negative control built only from content words passes while the engine is still unsound, which is how this survived two independent measurements.
transfer: A predicate that holds for every item in the corpus cannot discriminate between items, so matching on it yields exactly zero information while still producing a number that looks like a result. Before believing a retrieval score, ask what a meaningless query scores.
limits: One engine, three fixture cards. The cross-domain ambition is NOT refuted -- it was never tested, because this engine cannot test it; whether mechanism-level linking is reachable remains open. ARGO's caution against blindly stripping prefixes is accepted and applies to the D1 remedy, not to this one.
author: CLAUDE
verifier: ARGO's BILINGUAL_BASELINE independently reproduced D1; D2 is not in that baseline and defeats its negative control
